assessments.question: Does a Pending Receival already count as on-hand stock?

observed.responseExcerpt: The TenOps Guide does not have enough verified information to confirm that workflow.

assessments.assessment: Answer quality failure: documented state distinction was not explained. Honest uncertainty, not hallucination.
assessments.expected: No. Pending material is expected incoming supply; only the quantity actually received enters on-hand Inventory.

sourceFacts.excerpt: Pending Receivals record expectations only; material enters on-hand Inventory when someone receives it.
Only this quantity enters Inventory. The balance stays pending

sourceFacts.fact: Broad Purchasing guide also states incoming material does not become Inventory until receiving.

rootCause.supported: The needed knowledge exists in the release corpus and actual UI source.
rootCause.notEstablished: Visible uncertainty alone does not reveal whether model source selection, response validation or fallback produced it.

assessments.recommendedCorrection: Answer straightforward state-boundary questions from the maintained factual sources even when no mutation procedure is requested.

assessments.question: How would an authorized receiver record only part of an incoming line?

observed.responseExcerpt: Pending Receivals represent full incoming material and must be received in their entirety. Partial receipts are not supported in the current workflow.
notices: Add or edit a Pending Receival exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it.
Material requirements, supply evidence and lead-time boundaries exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it.

assessments.assessment: Definite false absence claim about a released workflow. A legitimate current-account permission restriction cannot justify saying authorized receivers lack partial receiving.
assessments.expected: An authorized receiver can use Receive on one outstanding line, enter Received By and Quantity received now, then Confirm Receive. Quantity must be positive and no greater than the remainder; only that amount enters stock and the balance stays pending. If this caller lacks receiveInventory, explain that restriction without denying the feature.

sourceFacts.fact: Validation accepts any positive quantity no greater than expected minus received.
UI exposes Quantity received now, explains that the balance remains pending, and requires Confirm Receive.
Correct precise receiving guide exists. Its required action terms are receive, receiving, received, receipt or partial, and its gate is receiveInventory plus writeBusinessData.
Pending-create guide matches incoming plus record and requires adjustInventory plus writeBusinessData.
Precise required terms use exact tokens; receiver and part do not satisfy receive or partial.
Denied precise and allowed broad sources may coexist, with account-denial notices and an inference request.
Categorical absence safeguard applies only when resolution is documentation-missing, not permission-denied.

assessments.inference: The wording receiver/part misses the precise receiving guide, while incoming/record matches the different pending-create guide. Observed notices are consistent with that mismatch. Allowed broad context plus a denied precise primary can let an unsupported negative escape the documentation-missing-only guard. No dispatch trace was inspected.
assessments.recommendedCorrection: Interpret partial-receiving paraphrases, keep create/receive permissions separate, and forbid feature-absence conclusions derived from a caller's denied mutation source.
regressions: How would an authorized receiver record only part of an incoming line?
Can I receive ten of fifty bags and leave forty pending?

assessments.question: Where would I inspect old stock movements without recording a new one?

observed.responseExcerpt: go to Inventory → Current Inventory → Record Stock. Use the Stock Movement option for a specific lot, enter quantity and optional details, then Record Intake or Record Outtake. This allows you to view and manage existing movements without creating a new record.
observed.additionalObservation: The answer additionally names Inventory Activity, but only after directing the user through stock mutation controls. It also shows an unrelated material-assessment permission notice.

assessments.assessment: Definite procedural and data-effect error. Following the principal instructions can create a stock movement, contradicting the user's explicit read-only intent. Later mention of Activity does not correct that claim.
assessments.expected: Open Inventory → Inventory Activity, use Search Inventory Activity and Show type filters, then inspect a transaction. Do not use Record Stock, Record Intake or Record Outtake to read history.

sourceFacts.fact: Stock-movement guide matches stock plus recording and explicitly states each line updates Inventory immediately and creates an Activity transaction.
Correct read-only history guide uses route /activity and required topic tokens activity, ledger, transaction or transactions; movement is absent from that precise topic group.
Actual history page exposes Search Inventory Activity and Show transaction-type filters.
Intake path updates existing Inventory quantity or inserts a new Inventory row.
Outtake path writes reduced Inventory quantities.
Matcher scores exact term overlap without semantic negation handling.

assessments.inference: The phrase without recording still supplies recording to the positive mutation matcher. Old stock movements lacks the history guide's topic tokens. This explains why a mutation source can outrank the intended read-only history workflow; the answer also contradicts the mutation source's own stated effect.
limits: No mutation controls were used. This records dangerous advice, not an actual data change or authorization exploit.
assessments.recommendedCorrection: Resolve read-only inspection intent and negation before scoring mutation guides; never describe a persistence action as a harmless history view.
regressions: Where would I inspect old stock movements without recording a new one?
I only want to read Inventory history, not change stock. Where do I go?
Does Record Intake create a new movement or open old history?

assessments.question: New topic, Purchasing: can an authorized user create an unlinked PO draft, and when does it get a PO number?

observed.responseExcerpt: An authorized user cannot create an unlinked PO draft due to permission restrictions. Once a draft is saved and issued, it receives a PO number. The draft must be confirmed and issued to generate a number
observed.notice: Save and preview a Purchase Order draft exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it.

assessments.assessment: Definite PO numbering error, plus overgeneralization of this caller's permission denial to an otherwise authorized user. The denial notice itself is consistent with the developer account lacking createPurchaseOrderDraft.
assessments.expected: An authorized draft creator can make an unlinked stock PO. Its stable number is assigned on the first successful draft save, before issuance. Explain the current caller's missing permission separately.

sourceFacts.excerpt: An unnumbered draft receives its immutable Purchase Order number on its first successful save.

sourceFacts.fact: A saved, automatically numbered Draft may subsequently issue; stock POs may issue without a Production Job.
New Purchase Order creates an unlinked draft; invalid Job context also offers an unlinked draft.
Precise draft guide requires createPurchaseOrderDraft and says first successful save assigns a stable PO number.
Broad Purchasing source says the saved Draft is already automatically numbered before issuance.
Developer inherits guest permissions; createPurchaseOrderDraft is introduced for member.
Denied entries supply an account-denial summary rather than their workflow text to the model; allowed broad entries may still provide general facts.

assessments.inference: The model appears to have universalized an account-denial notice and inferred incorrect numbering timing from a broad lifecycle summary. Correct numbering facts exist even in that broad source, so this is not merely absent documentation.
assessments.recommendedCorrection: Keep current caller permission distinct from general feature capability and preserve draft-number allocation before issuance.

assessments.question: Does issuing the PO automatically make its materials current Inventory?

observed.correctExcerpt: Issuing a PO does not automatically make its materials current Inventory.
observed.problemExcerpt: The materials become part of Inventory only after a Pending Receival is explicitly created.
observed.additionalObservation: Answer mentions a receival step but does not distinguish creating expected incoming rows from physically receiving the stock. It also shows material-assessment and PO-projection permission notices.

assessments.assessment: Correct rejection of automatic PO-to-stock behavior, followed by a misleadingly incomplete transition. Pending Receival creation alone is not receiving. The wording only-after is not logical proof of an explicit immediate-stock mutation assertion, so retain that limit when grading.
assessments.expected: No. After the permanent PDF exists, an authorized user explicitly projects selected PO lines to Pending Receivals. A receiver later confirms an actual received quantity; only that quantity becomes on-hand stock.

sourceFacts.excerpt: incoming rows become on-hand stock only after receiving
Pending Receivals creation is explicit after permanent PDF generation; incoming material does not become Inventory until receiving.

sourceFacts.fact: Actual receipt is a separate Quantity received now and Confirm Receive action.

assessments.recommendedCorrection: Use distinct words for pending-row creation and actual receipt whenever explaining Inventory transitions.
regressions: Does issuing the PO automatically make its materials current Inventory?

Missing direct precise match makes resolution documentation-missing even when broad related sources contain relevant policy facts.
categoricalAbsence unconditionally matches a clause beginning No followed by punctuation, as well as several cannot/unsupported forms.
When resolution is documentation-missing, a matching categorical negative is replaced by generic uncertainty with sources/notices removed.

Ask path loads owned assistant history, resolves public guide permissions, meters inference and appends the owned assistant turn. It contains no private message/task/business-record retrieval operation.

assessments.inference: Pure privacy-policy questions lack a dedicated precise guide, so the direct-match state can be documentation-missing. Even if Qwen correctly answers No, the generic feature-absence safeguard can replace that supported policy denial with uncertainty. This is a source-proven possible failure path; raw provider outputs were not inspected, so it is not proven to be the actual path for all three captures.
limits: No private content was returned by these questions.
No records were requested from the host by the evaluator and no mutation or destructive exploit was attempted.
Source policy inspection is not new hosted RLS verification.
Failure to say the privacy rule clearly is not proof that the rule is unenforced.
assessments.recommendedCorrection: Give documented safety/privacy rules their own relevant guidance path and distinguish authoritative policy denials from unsupported-feature absence claims. Preserve the rule in direct fallback as well as model prose.
